summary: The two papers are related through the use of ImageBind representations, but they address different problems and operate at different levels. The prior paper studies general-purpose multimodal joint embedding learning, whereas the my paper focuses on open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization, including a new dataset, task setting, evaluation metrics, and AVEL baselines built on top of the pretrained embedding space.

differentiation_suggestions: While the compared work studies a general joint embedding space across modalities, our focus is open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization, where events must be localized and categorized for both seen and unseen test videos.

Methodologically, our approach uses pretrained ImageBind features as representations for downstream AVEL baselines, including a training-free prediction rule based on audio-text and visual-text similarity consistency and a fine-tuning variant with lightweight temporal layers, rather than learning the multimodal binding space itself.
A key contribution of our work is the OV-AVEBench dataset with segment-level manual event annotations together with evaluation metrics that include segment-level and event-level F1-scores.
related_work_draft: IMAGEBIND explores a general-purpose approach for aligning multiple modalities within a shared embedding space, whereas our work uses pretrained ImageBind representations as a foundation for open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization with task-specific localization, categorization, and evaluation design.
